classification.difficultyReason: Use scaffolded normalisation and exponential integration, rearrange the CDF with a logarithm to obtain a general quantile formula, then substitute the three quartile probabilities.

answer.short: Decreasing, concave-up exponential curve from $(0,c)$ to $(1,\frac{c}{e})$, restricted to $0\le x\le1$.
answer.worked: For $c>0$, $f'(x)=-ce^{-x}<0$ and $f''(x)=ce^{-x}>0$. The curve decreases and is concave up, with $f(0)=c$ and $f(1)=\frac{c}{e}$.

children.prompt: Find a general equation for finding any percentile by setting $F(x)=p$.

answer.worked:
Set $F(x)=p$:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{e}{e-1}(1-e^{-x})&=p\\e^{-x}&=1-\frac{p(e-1)}{e}\\-x&=\ln\!\left(\frac{e-p(e-1)}{e}\right)\\x&=\ln\!\left(\frac{e}{e-p(e-1)}\right).\end{aligned}$$
Here $p$ is the cumulative probability, with $0\le p\le1$.

Substitute $p=\tfrac14$, $\tfrac12$ and $\tfrac34$ into the equation from part d:
$$\begin{aligned}Q_1&=\ln\!\left(\frac{e}{e-\frac14(e-1)}\right)=\ln\!\left(\frac{4e}{3e+1}\right),\\Q_2&=\ln\!\left(\frac{e}{e-\frac12(e-1)}\right)=\ln\!\left(\frac{2e}{e+1}\right),\\Q_3&=\ln\!\left(\frac{e}{e-\frac34(e-1)}\right)=\ln\!\left(\frac{4e}{e+3}\right).\end{aligned}$$
